data.hypothesis: Deduplicating and sorting blocked coordinates enables a sparse combinatorial path count when obstacle-pair work is below a grid scan. A contiguous one-dimensional row-major DP fallback avoids quadratic blocked-grid storage when the obstacle set is larger.
data.notes: Uses only input dimensions and unique obstacle count to choose the algorithm; no benchmark-specific assumptions. No commands run.
transformations: Replace the N-by-N blocked-cell matrix with a sorted, deduplicated contiguous obstacle list.
For fewer than N unique obstacles, count paths using factorial-based binomial coefficients and subtract paths whose first blocked cell is each obstacle.
Otherwise, use a row-major one-dimensional DP and advance through the sorted obstacle list to mark blocked cells.
